official.deadline_note: One call per year for all doctoral programmes; the 2026 window (24 August - 7 September 2026) has closed and all applicants were to be notified of decisions by the end of November 2026. No dates for the next annual round have been published; based on the annual pattern it is expected around late August 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2026 cycle - application window 24 August - 7 September 2026 for employment starting in 2027; next annual cycle not yet announced
official.status_note: The University states there is one application period each year for all of its doctoral programmes and that the next application period for salaried positions ran August 24 - September 7, 2026; that window has closed. The Studies Service instructions page (updated 30.9.2026) confirms decisions were to be communicated by the end of November 2026 and that successful applicants' names would be published on the Doctoral School website. The Recruitment System job ad for the 2026 call is now marked as ended/removed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The University of Helsinki does not collect tuition fees from doctoral researchers, and studies at the University are free.
benefits: A full-time employment contract with the University of Helsinki; the positions are designated as full-time work
Salary and social security, plus employee rights such as occupational health care, work facilities and equipment and other staff services
A six-month probationary period within which selected applicants without prior doctoral study rights must obtain the right to pursue a doctoral degree at the University of Helsinki
Access to Doctoral School travel support for conference travel through separate application calls (autumn 2026 call budget EUR 100,000)
No tuition fees charged to doctoral researchers
Ten four-year positions co-funded by the University of Helsinki Research Foundation and sixteen three-year R&D-funded positions are awarded from the same 2026 call, with no separate application
eligibility: The application is submitted by the deadline
The application is accompanied by all required attachments in the specified format
The applicant's research plan is relevant to the doctoral programme they are applying to
The applicant has supervision arrangements in place as per the doctoral programme's guidelines; all applicants must have a supervisor at the time of application
Applications and attachments are prepared in the language required by the doctoral programme
The length of the requested position corresponds to the durations of available positions in the programme
General eligibility for doctoral studies: a completed (or completed by the deadline) degree giving eligibility to doctoral studies, plus academic-level language skills proven in an accepted manner
Both current University of Helsinki doctoral researchers and new applicants planning doctoral studies are eligible to apply
requirements: A qualifying second-cycle (Master's) degree; programme-specific instructions require the master's degree to be completed and granted by the end of the application year
Supervision arrangements in place at the time of application, following the doctoral programme's guidelines
All attachments combined into a single PDF named Lastname_Firstname_application, maximum size 5 MB, font Arial/Calibri size 11 (or similar), line spacing minimum 1.15
Research plan on the University's template, maximum five pages; applications deviating from the template or page limits will be rejected
CV on the University's template, maximum three pages
Supervision plan on the University's template, maximum two pages, requiring the supervisor's signature
Copy of the Master's degree diploma and transcript of studies from every applicant, including those who already hold doctoral study rights or graduated from the University of Helsinki
Any use of artificial intelligence in preparing the application must be reported in the research plan
documents: Application form completed in the University of Helsinki electronic recruitment system
Supervision plan (University template, max 2 pages, supervisor's signature required)
Copy of the Master's degree diploma (scanned copy sufficient, certified copies not required at this stage)
Transcript of studies (master's, and doctoral studies too if already started)
selection_criteria: External experts appointed by the programme steering groups assess all eligible applications for three- to four-year positions on a common scale; an application must achieve at least 3/5 (good) in each criterion as an average from three assessors to proceed
Quality of the research plan - 50% weighting
Feasibility of the research plan (realistic achievability incl. target time, work plan, supervision arrangements and research environment, risks and mitigation) - 30% weighting
Competence of the applicant (CV, relevant experience, skills and competences) - 20% weighting
Doctoral programmes may conduct interviews to complement the external evaluation
For one- to two-year positions, assessment emphasises the feasibility of completing the research within the requested funding period
The doctoral programme steering group proposes selected applicants to the unit director, who makes the employment decision

University of Helsinki Research Foundation positions are evaluated on scientific excellence, interdisciplinarity and societal impact, ability to identify societal challenges, early research-career stage and feasibility of the research plan
coverage: Salary as a full-time university-employed doctoral researcher; the employment contract determines the exact duration and the start and end dates, and salary details are published in the call for applications
Social security, occupational health care, work facilities and equipment and other staff services that come with University employment
Doctoral studies themselves are free: the University of Helsinki does not collect tuition fees from doctoral researchers
Living and accommodation costs are the doctoral researcher's own responsibility and are not added to the position
Research-related expenses are generally not covered by the Doctoral School or doctoral programmes
Conference travel may be supported through separate Doctoral School and faculty travel-support calls
application_method: Submit the application and all attachments via the University of Helsinki electronic recruitment system (jobs.helsinki.fi)
The application form is open only during the annual application period; it closes at 11:59 PM on the final day
Select the doctoral programme you are applying to, and follow both the general and the doctoral programme-specific instructions

Answer all form sections: background information, doctoral study rights, employment contract preferences (start date and length in years), thesis project, supervisor(s), master's degree and possible interruptions
General questions go to phd-positions@helsinki.fi; questions about research plans, supervisors or programmes go directly to the doctoral programme
official.application_route: Apply once per year through the University of Helsinki's electronic recruitment system during the annual autumn window, choosing one doctoral programme and following both the general and programme-specific instructions
official.study_mode: Full-time (positions are designated as full-time work)
official.international_eligibility: International applicants are eligible; the University states that one fourth of its doctoral researchers are international students and that completing a doctoral degree in English is possible in all doctoral programmes. No citizenship restriction is published for this call.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must apply to one of the University's doctoral programmes and their research plan must be relevant to that programme; only one university-funded doctoral researcher position may be applied for in the call. Programme-specific rules (e.g. available position lengths, application language, additional eligibility criteria) apply.
official.research_requirement: A research plan prepared on the University's template (maximum five pages) together with the supervisor, with supervision arrangements already in place at the time of application; use of AI in preparing the application must be reported in the research plan
official.duration: Positions are always at least 12 months long and full years in duration. The majority are 3-4-year positions for applicants in the early stages of their doctoral work; some programmes also offer 1-2-year positions for later stages, with a 6-12-month exception for specialised training related to doctoral work in medicine, dentistry or veterinary medicine. Employment can start no earlier than 1 January of the year following the call and, in the 2026 call, had to commence during 2027.
official.description: The University of Helsinki Doctoral School (UHDS) provides annual funding for doctoral researcher positions in doctoral programmes. These doctoral researcher positions are designated as full-time work. The aim is that the university-funded doctoral researchers will pursue a post-graduate doctoral degree, which should be completed within four years.
official.program_type: University-funded salaried doctoral researcher position (full-time employment)
official.english_requirement: Academic-level skills in Finnish, Swedish or English must be proven in an accepted way. For English: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with 6.0 in every section; TOEFL iBT total 92 with at least 22 in writing (tests taken before 21 January 2026) or total 4.5 with at least 4 in each section (tests from 21 January 2026); Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency at pass level; PTE Academic overall 68 with at least 61 in writing; National Certificate of Language Proficiency (YKI) level 5 in all sub-tests; or an exempting educational background (e.g. a degree completed in English in a listed country). Scores must remain valid for the whole application period.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an employment call, not a grant: winning means a full-time salary as a University of Helsinki employee while you finish a PhD in one of the University's 14 doctoral programmes. The window is short and annual - roughly two weeks in late August - and everything hinges on preparation done months in advance, especially securing a supervisor and building the template documents. Doctoral study itself is free, but the salary must carry your living and accommodation costs in Helsinki, and research materials and conference travel are not funded by the position (travel has its own separate, competitive Doctoral School calls).
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career master's graduates, or current University of Helsinki doctoral researchers, who can line up a willing supervisor before August and want a salaried, full-time four-year doctorate in any UH discipline.
application_readiness_checklist: Email a potential supervisor months before the window opens; supervision arrangements must already be in place when you apply
Download the official research plan, CV and supervision plan templates and follow their structure and page limits exactly
Get the supervision plan signed by your supervisor early - it is the single most common late stumble
Locate your master's diploma and transcripts (and doctoral transcripts if you have already started) before the window opens
Check the doctoral programme's own instructions for the permitted application language, position lengths and any extra criteria
Merge everything into one PDF named Lastname_Firstname_application, kept under 5 MB, in Arial/Calibri 11 with 1.15 line spacing
Submit at least a day early: no questions about the application or form are answered after 16:00 EEST on the final day
common_rejection_risks: Exceeding the research plan's five-page limit or the three-page CV limit - the University states plainly that applications deviating from template instructions will be rejected
A supervision plan missing the supervisor's signature, or the Thessa supervision plan used instead of the required attachment
Leaving out the diploma or transcript because you already hold doctoral study rights - they are required from every applicant regardless
A research plan that does not match the doctoral programme you selected, or a requested position length the programme does not offer
Submitting more than one application (only the most recently dated one is counted, and the rules say only one position may be applied for)
For applicants without study rights: failing to obtain the doctoral study right within six months of starting employment, which costs the position during probation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living and accommodation costs in the Helsinki metropolitan area, which the University describes as relatively high in European terms and which the doctoral researcher is expected to cover from the salary; research expenses such as special equipment, fee-based materials or bespoke infrastructure, which the Doctoral School and programmes generally do not cover; and conference travel, which only succeeds through separate travel-support calls. Relocation support is not part of this call (it is a feature of the separate RESDOC MSCA COFUND positions).
document_audit: The three template documents must keep their original structure and margins - altered margins or extra pages lead to rejection
One combined PDF only, named Lastname_Firstname_application, maximum 5 MB; separate uploads or oversized files break the format requirement
The supervision plan needs a real supervisor signature, and the Thessa supervision plan explicitly does not substitute for it
Diploma scans are fine, but they must come from every applicant, including University of Helsinki graduates
Transcripts must cover both master's and doctoral studies if doctoral studies have started
Attachments cannot be supplemented after the deadline, and previous years' attachments are grounds for rejection
Any AI assistance used while writing the research plan must be disclosed inside the research plan itself
alerts: Timing trap: the call opens and closes in about two weeks in late August, but the work behind it (supervisor, templates, signatures) takes months - treat it as a year-round project
Positions cannot start before 1 January of the year after the call, so plan your funding and any relocation around a January-March start
If you do not yet hold doctoral study rights you must win them in a separate study-right call (by spring 2027 at the latest for the 2026 round) or lose the position during the six-month probation
Total University funding for the same doctoral project may not exceed four years, so check what you have already used

Ten four-year University of Helsinki Research Foundation positions and sixteen three-year R&D-funded positions are allocated from this same application - a strong three-year application can be forwarded without any further effort from you
The Doctoral School cannot advise on research plans or supervisors; email phd-positions@helsinki.fi only for process questions and go to the programme for anything substantive
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application through the University of Helsinki recruitment system during the annual window; the programme steering group scores and ranks applications with external assessors and proposes candidates to the unit director, who signs off the employment.
